subject: Re: Burst capacity — slab exceptions and cooldown flexibility
messages:
From: Katie Li <katie@fintechcorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fintechcorp.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity questions: burst slab and cooldown for Dedicated pool

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the Dedicated pool looks promising. We have a couple of follow-ups from infra and finance before we can sign:

- Month-end batch runs spike our token throughput for ~90 minutes; we need headroom above our reserved commit to avoid dropped jobs.
- We like the idea of a burst add-on, but we need clarity on: what constitutes a "burst unit" (GPU-minutes? vGPU slots?), how the surge rate is calculated, and how long the cooldown is after a burst.
- During the busiest 3 hours (two month-ends per quarter), we may need two separate bursts within a 30-minute window. Your standard cooldown (60m) would prevent that. Is there an exception or a "double-burst" option?

Can you send a clear pricing example for: baseline commit (16x A100-equivalent GPUs), one 60-minute burst, and then a follow-up 20-minute burst within 30 minutes? Also please attach any capacity/throughput worksheet you used in the demo.

Appreciate it — if we can chart a deterministic cost path and a short-term exception for month-end, procurement can finish the PO.

Regards,
Katie Li
Head of Platform Engineering
FinTech Corp

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Katie Li <katie@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity questions: burst slab and cooldown for Dedicated pool

Katie — great to hear from you, and thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a capacity worksheet and a concise pricing summary to make numbers explicit (attachments). Below are the concrete answers and a suggested one-time exception for month-end.

How we meter burst: we bill burst usage as GPU-minutes (per-GPU per-minute) using the same GPU type as your Dedicated commit; the UI shows the equivalent GPUT-minutes consumed. Surge rate: defined as a multiplier of your baseline per-GPU-minute rate. Examples below use your baseline per-GPU-minute price.

Standard proposal (examples):
- Baseline commit: 16 GPUs reserved (paid monthly).
- Single 60-minute burst: charged at 5x baseline per-GPU-minute for the first 30 minutes, then 2.5x for the remainder of that burst (to reflect elastic taper).
- Cooldown: default 60 minutes after a burst where automatic re-burst is rate-limited (prevents runaway).

Double-burst option (what we can offer):
- For your month-end windows: we can offer a temporary "double-burst" exception allowing one additional burst within 45 minutes of the first, at a reduced surge multiplier of 3x for that follow-up burst (vs. standard 5x).
- Limitations: applies only to two occurrences per calendar month unless otherwise expanded; requires a 3-month committed add-on purchase for the burst pool.

Discounts: 20% off burst multipliers for the first 3 months with a 6-month review. If you want a higher discount cap (we can discuss up to 30% subject to exec approval).

Next steps: can you confirm your expected GPU-minutes for the baseline and the two burst windows (I flagged this in the attached sheet)? Once we have that we can produce a line-item term sheet and a DocuSign link for approval.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Katie Li <katie@fintechcorp.com>

Date: 2027-06-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity questions: burst slab and cooldown for Dedicated pool

Aditya, thanks for the table — that helps a lot. Two follow-ups from infra and our finance PM:

1) Can you confirm the sustained throughput guarantee during/after a burst? Our pipeline performs short-lived concurrent jobs; we need a floor (e.g., at least 2x baseline throughput for the first 6 hours) so orchestrator timeouts don't cascade.
2) For the double-burst: the reduced multiplier (3x) is workable, but we need the option to request an ad-hoc "extra burst" if the first one is still draining queues. How fast is manual approval (if required)?

If you can get the sustained throughput guarantee and a fast path for approval documented, we'll route to procurement. Please also include the HubSpot deal id or the doc link for legal.

Regards,
Katie

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Capacity questions: burst slab and cooldown for Dedicated pool

Rishi / Lauren — forwarding FinTech's follow-ups. Quick internal notes:

- They want a sustained throughput floor (2x baseline for first 6 hours). Operationally, that maps to reserving a soft headroom pool that we guarantee for the window. Pricing impact: adds ~12% to the burst cost for reserved surge capacity.
- Double-burst to be allowed as a month-end exception with 3x multiplier for follow-up; procurement will want response time SLA for manual approvals (we should commit to <2 hours for pre-planned month-end exceptions).
- Discount: offering 20% is our starting point; if we push to 25–30% we need approval from sales leadership.

Can we confirm if we can author a one-page addendum that locks the month-end exception and the throughput floor, and commit to a 2-hour manual approval SLA? If yes, I'll send the revised term sheet and get legal looped.

-Aditya

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Katie Li <katie@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Updated offer: month-end double-burst exception + throughput floor (term sheet attached)

Katie — thanks for the quick responses. Per internal alignment, here's an updated, actionable offer that we can put on DocuSign today: 

1) Baseline commit: 16 GPUs (A100-equivalent), monthly committed pool (same as discussed).
2) Burst pricing: standard surge multiplier 5x for first 30 minutes, 2.5x thereafter for single bursts.
3) Month-end double-burst exception: one additional burst within 45 minutes at 3x multiplier (reduced follow-up rate). Applies up to two month-end windows per quarter.
4) Sustained throughput guarantee: for approved month-end windows we will reserve a soft headroom equivalent to 2x baseline throughput for up to 6 hours. This is applied as reserved burst capacity and carries a +12% cost uplift on the consumed burst minutes.
5) Approval SLA: manual exception approvals for pre-scheduled month-end windows — guaranteed response in <2 hours during business days. Emergency ad-hoc approvals can be requested; we aim to respond within 4 hours.
6) Discounts: 20% off the burst multipliers for the first 3 months. We can entertain a 25% cap with a short exec sign-off; anything beyond requires legal and finance review.

I've attached the revised term sheet (revised_term_sheet.docx) and included the HubSpot deal link and DocuSign URL above. If this matches your requirements I will open the DocuSign and route to your procurement contact.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
